q: Under a stores contract, stores of the value of Rs 4,75,000 remain in arrear of supply and are supplied 5 weeks late. Liquidated damages at 0.5% of the value of the stores in arrear per week of delay amount to:
e: Liquidated damages = 0.5 percent per week x 5 weeks x Rs 4,75,000 = 2.5 percent x 4,75,000 = Rs 11,875.

q: Within the annual procurement target of 25% from Micro and Small Enterprises, the sub-target for MSEs owned by women entrepreneurs is:
e: Within the 25 percent annual procurement target from MSEs, the sub-target for MSEs owned by women entrepreneurs is 3 percent, as per the Public Procurement Policy for MSEs.

q: A supplier's bill for stores amounts to Rs 8,75,000. The advance payment admissible at 98% of the bill value, against the inspection certificate and despatch documents, is:
e: Advance payment = 98 percent of Rs 8,75,000 = 0.98 x 8,75,000 = Rs 8,57,500, against inspection certificate and despatch documents.

q: A supplier claiming to be a Class-I local supplier under the Public Procurement (Preference to Make in India) Order states the local content of the item offered by him. The local content so claimed is:

options.A: Self-certified by the supplier himself, subject to verification and audit as prescribed
options.C: Certified by RDSO in all cases

e: Local content claimed by a Class-I local supplier under the Make in India Order is self-certified by the supplier, subject to verification and audit as prescribed.

q: The re-order level of an item is 1,950 units. The average consumption is 135 units per week and the average lead time is 9 weeks. The minimum stock level of the item is:
e: Minimum stock level = 1,950 - (135 x 9) = 1,950 - 1,215 = 735 units.

q: A consuming department places a demand on a stores depot for an item. For the procurement of stores against the demands so received, an 'indent' is placed by:

options.B: The Accounts office, on the depot
options.C: The purchaser of scrap, on the depot

e: For procurement against demands received from consuming departments, the indent is placed by the depot or purchase office.

q: The re-order level of an item is 2,150 units and the re-order quantity is 1,250 units. The minimum consumption is 85 units per week and the minimum lead time is 6 weeks. The maximum stock level of the item is:
While the Stores Budget of a zonal railway is being framed, the headquarters office consolidates the budget from:

options.A: The requirements furnished by the stores depots and the consuming departments
options.B: The estimates sent directly by the suppliers of stores
options.C: The Stores Budget of the previous year, without any change
options.D: The assessment made by the stock verifiers during stock verification

e: The Stores Budget is consolidated at headquarters from the requirements furnished by the stores depots and the consuming departments.

q: The maximum consumption of an item is 235 units per week, its normal consumption is 185 units per week and the lead time is 7 weeks. The safety (buffer) stock to be provided for the item is:
e: Safety stock = (maximum consumption - normal consumption) x lead time = (235 - 185) x 7 = 50 x 7 = 350 units.

q: A supplier on whom liquidated damages are levied for delayed supply contends that the damages should be worked out on the total value of his purchase order, including the stores he supplied in time. Liquidated damages for delayed supply are actually levied on:

options.A: The total value of the purchase order, irrespective of the quantity supplied in time
options.B: The value of the stores remaining in arrear of supply, for the period of delay
options.C: The amount of the security deposit furnished by the supplier
options.D: The value of the stores actually supplied by the supplier

e: Liquidated damages are levied on the value of stores remaining in arrear of supply for the period of delay, not on stores supplied in time, as per the GCC for supply.

q: A supplier fails to supply 925 units of stores contracted at Rs 76 per unit. A risk purchase of the same quantity is made at Rs 94 per unit. The extra cost recoverable from the defaulting supplier is:
e: Extra cost of risk purchase = (Rs 94 - Rs 76) x 925 = Rs 18 x 925 = Rs 16,650, recoverable from the defaulting supplier.

q: Liquidated damages are being recovered from a supplier for delayed supplies under a stores contract, the levy being 0.5% of the value of the stores in arrear for each week of delay. The total recovery on this account cannot exceed:
e: Total liquidated damages recovery cannot exceed 10 percent of the contract value, as per the GCC for supply.

q: Eleven wagons loaded with stores are detained at a depot for 4 days beyond the free time allowed for unloading. Demurrage is payable at Rs 650 per wagon per day. The total demurrage payable is:
e: Total demurrage = 11 wagons x 4 days x Rs 650 per wagon per day = Rs 28,600.

q: The annual consumption of a stores item doubles, the cost of placing an order and the inventory carrying cost per unit remaining the same. Its Economic Order Quantity will:

options.B: Increase by about 41 per cent, i.e. in the ratio of the square root of two, and not double

e: EOQ varies with the square root of annual consumption, so doubling consumption raises EOQ by the square root of 2, about 41 percent, and not double.

q: A purchase order is placed on a supplier for stores valued at Rs 11,40,000. The security deposit prescribed under the contract at 5 per cent of the order value works out to:
e: Security Deposit = 5 percent of Rs 11,40,000 = 0.05 x 11,40,000 = Rs 57,000.

q: The organisation which approves sources for safety and critical stores items, and whose specifications govern the procurement of such items, is the RDSO, which stands for:
e: RDSO stands for Research Designs and Standards Organisation, which approves sources and lays down specifications for safety and critical stores items.

q: A stores depot issues 815 units of an item whose book rate is Rs 47 per unit. The value of the issue debited to the consuming department is:
e: Value of issue = 815 units x Rs 47 per unit = Rs 38,305, debited to the consuming department at the book rate.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. An item whose unit price is very high must be placed in the 'A' category of ABC analysis even when its annual consumption is negligible.
2. An item priced low per unit may still be placed in the 'A' category when it is consumed in very large quantities, ABC classification being based on annual consumption value.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: ABC classification is based on annual consumption value, so a low-priced item consumed in very large quantities can be A category - statement 2 only; high unit price alone with negligible consumption does not make it A.

q: A stores depot issues 425 units of an item, whose book rate is Rs 88 per unit, to an outside party. Departmental charges are leviable at 10 per cent of the book value. The total amount recoverable from the party is:
e: Book value = 425 x Rs 88 = Rs 37,400; with departmental charges at 10 percent, recoverable amount = 37,400 x 1.10 = Rs 41,140.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The buffer (safety) stock of an item is drawn upon only when the consumption exceeds the normal rate or the replenishment of stock is delayed.
2. The buffer (safety) stock of an item forms a part of its normal cycle stock and is consumed in every replenishment cycle.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Buffer (safety) stock is drawn upon only when consumption exceeds the normal rate or replenishment is delayed - statement 1 only; it is not part of normal cycle stock consumed every cycle.

q: A depot holds 3,150 units of an item. The book rate of the item is revised from Rs 64 to Rs 56 per unit. The decrease in the value of the stock in hand, which is adjusted through the Stock Adjustment Account, is:
e: Decrease in stock value = 3,150 units x (Rs 64 - Rs 56) = 3,150 x Rs 8 = Rs 25,200, adjusted through the Stock Adjustment Account.

q: A supplier treats the delivery period stipulated in his purchase order as a mere target and supplies the stores well after it, without seeking any extension. In a stores contract, the delivery period stipulated in the purchase order is:

options.A: Only an indicative target for the supplier
options.B: Of the essence of the contract
options.C: Extendable by the supplier at his own discretion

e: In a stores contract the delivery period stipulated in the purchase order is of the essence of the contract, and the supplier cannot extend it at his own discretion.

q: The opening debit balance under Purchase Suspense of a railway is Rs 27 lakh. During the month, stores bills amounting to Rs 68 lakh are paid and material worth Rs 59 lakh is received at the depots and linked with the bills. The closing balance under Purchase Suspense is:
e: Closing Purchase Suspense = 27 + 68 - 59 = Rs 36 lakh debit balance.

q: In an e-auction of scrap on IREPS, a bidder who wishes to better the prevailing highest bid for a lot must ensure that his successive bid:

options.A: Exceeds the previous highest bid at least by the bid increment specified for the lot
options.B: Is equal to the reserve price of the lot
options.C: Is accompanied by a fresh earnest money deposit
options.D: Is approved in advance by the Tender Committee

e: In IREPS scrap e-auction, each successive bid must exceed the previous highest bid at least by the bid increment specified for the lot.

q: The opening balance of stores of a railway is Rs 92 lakh and the closing balance is Rs 68 lakh. The average stock held during the year is:
e: Average stock = (opening + closing) / 2 = (Rs 92 lakh + Rs 68 lakh) / 2 = Rs 80 lakh.

q: A supplier, instead of depositing cash, offers to furnish the Security Deposit required under his stores contract in another form permitted by the contract. The Security Deposit may be furnished by the supplier in the form of:

options.B: Cash deposit, bank guarantee, fixed deposit receipt or recovery from his bills, as stipulated in the contract
options.D: A personal surety bond of two railway employees

e: Security Deposit may be furnished as cash deposit, bank guarantee, fixed deposit receipt or recovery from bills, as stipulated in the contract.

q: The opening balance of stores of a railway is Rs 74 lakh, receipts of stores during the year are Rs 2.58 crore and issues during the year are Rs 2.42 crore. The closing balance of stores is:
e: Closing balance = 74 + 258 - 242 = Rs 90 lakh (opening Rs 74 lakh plus receipts Rs 2.58 crore minus issues Rs 2.42 crore).

q: In the course of a week, a stores depot receives stores by purchase from a supplier, stores manufactured in a railway workshop, stores transferred from another depot and stores returned by a department. A Receipt Note is prepared by the depot for stores received from:

options.A: All these sources — purchases, workshop manufacture, transfers from other depots and returns from departments/works

e: A Receipt Note is prepared for stores received from all sources - outside purchases, workshop manufacture, transfers from other depots and returns from departments or works.

q: The annual consumption of an item is 10,000 units. The cost of placing one order is Rs 80 and the inventory carrying cost is Rs 10 per unit per year. The total of the ordering cost and the carrying cost per year, when orders are placed in Economic Order Quantities, is:
e: EOQ = square root of (2 x 10,000 x 80 / 10) = 400 units; ordering cost = (10,000 / 400) x 80 = Rs 2,000 and carrying cost = (400 / 2) x 10 = Rs 2,000, total Rs 4,000 per year.

q: On completion of stock verification of an item, the stock sheet showing the difference between the physical and book balances is put up to the stockholder, who signs it:

options.A: As an admission of personal liability in all cases
options.B: In token of his having seen and noted the difference recorded
options.C: Only when an excess is found in the stock
options.D: Only when directed by the Railway Board

e: The stockholder signs the stock sheet in token of having seen and noted the difference recorded on stock verification, not as an admission of personal liability in all cases.

q: During stock verification, a shortage of 33 units of an item is found. The book rate of the item is Rs 385 per unit. The value of the shortage to be accounted for is:
e: Value of shortage = 33 units x Rs 385 per unit = Rs 12,705.

q: At the close of the financial year, certain stores paid for by a railway are still in transit and have not reached its depots. In the stores balance of the railway, these stores are reflected:

options.A: Through the debit balance outstanding under Purchase Suspense
options.B: As a liability of the railway
options.C: Through the credit balance under Sales Suspense
options.D: They are excluded from the stores balance altogether

e: Stores paid for but still in transit at year end are reflected in the stores balance through the debit balance outstanding under Purchase Suspense.

q: An item has an Economic Order Quantity of 780 units and a safety stock of 230 units. Under the EOQ system with a uniform rate of consumption, the average inventory of the item held is:
e: Average inventory = EOQ / 2 + safety stock = 780 / 2 + 230 = 390 + 230 = 620 units.

q:
A purchase office is fixing the stocking norms for an imported stores item and for a comparable indigenous item. Consider the following statements:
1. Imported stores generally take longer to procure than indigenous stores.
2. For that reason, imported items are provided with comparatively higher safety stock and coverage than indigenous items.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct - imported stores generally take longer to procure, so imported items are given comparatively higher safety stock and coverage than indigenous items.

q: The AAC of an item is 10,500 units. Coverage for three months is required to be provided. The stock in hand is 725 units and the dues (quantity already on order) are 400 units. The quantity to be ordered is:
e: Quantity required for 3 months = (10,500 / 12) x 3 = 2,625 units; quantity to order = 2,625 - 725 stock - 400 dues = 1,500 units.

q: The ABC categorisation of the stores items of a depot was carried out several years ago. Since then, the consumption pattern of many items and their prices have changed materially, but the categories have never been looked at again. The correct course in regard to the ABC analysis is to:

options.A: Revise the categories only once in ten years, as originally laid down
options.B: Revise the categorisation only when an item is deleted from the Priced Vocabulary
options.C: Leave the categories permanently as first fixed, revision not being permitted
options.D: Revise the categorisation periodically, as the consumption pattern and the prices of items change

e: ABC categorisation must be revised periodically as consumption patterns and prices change; categories are not left permanently as first fixed.

q: The annual consumption of an item is 2,880 units. The cost of placing one order is Rs 90 and the inventory carrying cost is Rs 4 per unit per year. The Economic Order Quantity of the item is:
e: EOQ = square root of (2 x 2,880 x 90 / 4) = square root of 1,29,600 = 360 units.

q: While evaluating the offers received against a stores tender, the purchase office refers to the lowest acceptable tenderer as 'L1'. In this usage, 'L1' denotes the tenderer:

options.A: Whose evaluated offer is the lowest
options.B: Who submitted his tender first among all the tenderers
options.C: Who is borne at serial number one of the approved list of suppliers
options.D: Who has quoted for the largest quantity in the tender

e: In tender evaluation, L1 denotes the tenderer whose evaluated offer is the lowest.

q:
Consider the following statements about purchases through the Government e-Marketplace (GeM), as per the General Financial Rules:
1. For purchases up to Rs 25,000, direct purchase without price comparison is permissible.
2. For purchases above Rs 25,000 and up to Rs 5 lakh, the buyer compares the offerings of at least three sellers/brands available on GeM and purchases from the lowest (L1) among them.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Under GFR Rule 149 as amended, GeM direct purchase without comparison is allowed up to Rs 50,000; above Rs 50,000 up to Rs 10 lakh purchase is through the lowest-priced seller among at least three manufacturers; above Rs 10 lakh, online bidding/reverse auction is mandatory. (Source: Department of Expenditure, Ministry of Finance, GFR amendment dated 10.07.2024.)

q: A supplier's bill for stores amounts to Rs 5,60,000. Advance payment at 98% of the bill value has been made against the inspection certificate and despatch documents. The balance amount payable after the material is received, inspected and accepted at the destination depot is:
e: Balance payable = total bill minus 98 percent advance = 2 percent of Rs 5,60,000 = Rs 11,200, payable after receipt, inspection and acceptance at destination.

q: A Proprietary Article Certificate (PAC), on the basis of which an item is procured from a single source, certifies that:

options.A: The item is of a proprietary nature, manufactured by a particular firm, and no suitable substitute manufactured by another firm is available
options.B: The item is the cheapest one available in the market
options.C: The supplying firm is registered with the Railway Board
options.D: The item is exempt from inspection before despatch

e: A Proprietary Article Certificate certifies that the item is proprietary, manufactured by a particular firm, and no suitable substitute from another firm is available, justifying single-source procurement.

q: The Turnover Ratio of the stores of a railway falls from 0.32 to 0.24 over a year, other things remaining the same. This fall in the ratio generally indicates:

options.A: Excessive stocking of stores in the depots of the railway
options.B: A larger proportion of dead surplus in the stock held
options.C: Better turnover of the capital locked up in stores
options.D: Heavy outstanding balances under Purchase Suspense

e: Turnover Ratio here is stock balance relative to issues; a fall from 0.32 to 0.24 means less stock is held per rupee of issues, indicating better turnover of capital locked up in stores.

q: The maximum consumption of an item is 165 units per week, its normal consumption is 115 units per week and the lead time for its procurement is 6 weeks. The safety (buffer) stock to be provided for the item is:
e: Safety stock = (maximum consumption - normal consumption) x lead time = (165 - 115) x 6 = 50 x 6 = 300 units.

q: A supplier has defaulted in supplying stores against a purchase order and the Railway proposes to make a risk purchase against him. Before the risk purchase is effected, the Railway is required to:

options.A: Obtain the permission of the lowest tenderer in the original tender
options.B: File a suit against the supplier in a court of law
options.C: Refund the security deposit of the supplier in full
options.D: Serve a notice on the defaulting supplier calling upon him to supply the stores, failing which the purchase will be made at his risk and cost

e: Before effecting a risk purchase, the Railway must serve notice on the defaulting supplier to supply the stores, failing which purchase will be made at his risk and cost, as per the GCC for supply.

q: A depot is fixing the buffer stock of two items: a vital safety item, whose stock-out can affect the safe running of trains, and a high-value 'A' category item, in every unit of which a large amount of capital is locked up. The correct approach is to:

options.A: Keep the buffer stock of both items equally tight
options.B: Keep the buffer stock of the vital item comparatively generous and that of the 'A' category item comparatively tight
options.C: Keep the buffer stock of the vital item comparatively tight and that of the 'A' category item comparatively generous
options.D: Keep the buffer stock of both items equally generous

e: Buffer stock of a vital safety item is kept comparatively generous to avoid stock-out affecting safe train running, while that of a high-value A category item is kept comparatively tight to limit locked-up capital.

q: An item has an Economic Order Quantity of 720 units and a safety stock of 240 units. If the inventory carrying cost is Rs 18 per unit per year, the annual carrying cost of the average inventory held under the EOQ system with a uniform rate of consumption is:
e: Average inventory = 720 / 2 + 240 = 600 units; annual carrying cost = 600 x Rs 18 = Rs 10,800.

q: A purchase order does not prescribe any pre-despatch inspection of the stores. The supplier contends that, the order being silent, no inspection of the material is necessary at all. The correct position is that the material supplied is inspected:

options.A: By RDSO in every such case
options.B: By the supplier's own staff, whose certificate is final
options.C: By the consignee on receipt at destination, before the material is accepted into stock
options.D: Not at all, inspection being wholly dispensed with

e: Where no pre-despatch inspection is prescribed, the material is inspected by the consignee on receipt at destination before it is accepted into stock.

q: An item which was earlier procured only occasionally against specific demands is now required regularly by the consuming departments, and it is decided to keep it in regular stock in the depot. The item is treated as a 'stock item' of the depot when:

options.A: It has been held in the depot for more than 24 months
options.B: It is regularly stocked in the depot for meeting demands, bears a Price Ledger (PL) number and has an AAC fixed for it
options.C: It is purchased only once for a specific work
options.D: It is supplied free of cost by a contractor

e: An item is a stock item when it is regularly stocked in the depot for meeting demands, bears a Price Ledger number and has an AAC fixed for it.

q: The average consumption of an item is 95 units per day and the lead time for its procurement is 8 days. The consumption of the item during the lead time is:
e: Lead time consumption = average consumption x lead time = 95 units per day x 8 days = 760 units.

q: The primary object of taking Earnest Money Deposit from tenderers in a stores tender is to:

options.A: Meet the cost of advertising the tender
options.B: Pay the inspection charges of the material
options.C: Finance the purchase of the stores in advance
options.D: Ensure that the tenderer keeps his offer open during its validity and honours the order, if placed on him

e: Earnest Money Deposit is taken to ensure the tenderer keeps his offer open during its validity and honours the order if placed on him.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In a limited tender for stores, invitations to tender are sent only to firms borne on the approved list of suppliers for the item.
2. In an open tender for stores, only firms registered with the Railways are permitted to submit offers.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Under the Stores Code, a limited tender is confined to firms borne on the approved list of suppliers for the item, whereas an open tender is advertised publicly and any firm, registered or not, may offer; hence statement 1 alone is correct.

q: The maximum consumption of an item is 145 units per week and the maximum lead time for its procurement is 6 weeks. The re-order level of the item is:
e: Re-order level = maximum consumption x maximum lead time = 145 x 6 = 870 units.

q: The equipment for which costly insurance spares are held in a depot is itself condemned and scrapped, and the spares are not required for any other equipment on the railway. The insurance spares are then:

options.A: Retained in stock indefinitely, whatever happens
options.B: Issued free of cost to the depot staff
options.C: Reviewed, and if they are not required for any other equipment, declared surplus and disposed of

e: Insurance spares are held only for the equipment they insure; once that equipment is condemned and the spares serve no other equipment, they are reviewed, declared surplus and disposed of under the Stores Code provisions for surplus stores.

q: Two losses of stores come to notice in a depot. In the first case, the loss occurred despite the exercise of all due care and precaution by the custodian; in the second, the loss was caused by the custodian's own negligence. The correct treatment of the two cases is:

options.A: The loss is recovered from the custodian in both the cases
options.B: The loss is recovered from the custodian in neither case
options.C: In the first case the custodian is not held personally liable, while in the second case the loss is recoverable from him
options.D: In the first case the loss is recoverable from the custodian, while in the second case it is not

e: A custodian is personally liable for a loss of stores only where it results from his negligence or want of due care; a loss occurring despite all due care is written off under sanction and is not recovered from him.

q: The opening debit balance under Purchase Suspense of a railway is Rs 16 lakh. During the month, stores bills amounting to Rs 38 lakh are paid and material worth Rs 57 lakh is received at the depots and linked with the bills. The closing balance under Purchase Suspense is:

options.A: A debit balance of Rs 3 lakh
options.B: Nil, the account being fully cleared
options.C: A debit balance of Rs 9 lakh
options.D: A credit balance of Rs 3 lakh

e: Closing Purchase Suspense = opening debit 16 + bills paid 38 - material received and linked 57 = minus Rs 3 lakh, i.e. a credit balance of Rs 3 lakh.

q: Material is delivered by a supplier at the gate of a stores depot and a receipt is given to him for the material so delivered. That receipt is:

options.A: Final, the material being treated as accepted at the gate itself
options.B: Only provisional; the material is finally accepted only after inspection and issue of the receipt note
options.C: Followed by payment of the full bill amount at the gate
options.D: Not recorded anywhere in the depot records

e: The receipt given at the depot gate is only a provisional acknowledgement of delivery; stores are finally accepted only after inspection and issue of the receipt note, as per Stores Code receipt procedure.

q: A depot holds 500 units of an item at a book rate of Rs 22 per unit. Fresh receipts of 300 units at Rs 34 per unit and 200 units at Rs 44 per unit are taken into stock. The revised book (average) rate of the item will be:
e: Revised average rate = (500 x 22 + 300 x 34 + 200 x 44) / 1000 = 30,000 / 1000 = Rs 30 per unit, the book rate being the weighted average of stock and fresh receipts.

q: Advance payment of up to 98% of the value of stores has been made to a supplier against the inspection certificate and despatch documents, before the material is received at destination. In the books of the railway, this advance is initially accounted for under:
e: Payment made before receipt of material, such as 98 per cent against inspection certificate and despatch documents, is initially debited to Purchase Suspense and cleared when the material is received and linked with the bill.

q: Which of the following correctly brings out the distinction between an 'indent' and a 'purchase order' in stores procedure?

options.A: An indent is an internal demand placed for the procurement of stores, whereas a purchase order is the order placed on a supplier for their supply
options.B: An indent is an order placed on a supplier, whereas a purchase order is an internal demand for stores
options.C: An indent is a demand for stores required immediately, whereas a purchase order is for stores required in future
options.D: An indent is a document issued by the Accounts Department, whereas a purchase order is issued by the supplier

e: An indent is the internal demand raised for procurement of stores, while a purchase order is the formal order placed on the supplier; the two documents arise at different stages of Stores Code procedure.

q: The AAC of an item is 5,760 units. The stock in hand is 900 units and the dues (quantity already on order) are 300 units. The coverage available for the item is:
e: Monthly consumption = 5760 / 12 = 480 units; coverage = (stock 900 + dues 300) / 480 = 1200 / 480 = 2.5 months.

q: Debit balances under Purchase Suspense have remained outstanding in the books of a railway for a long time without clearance. Such long-outstanding balances generally indicate that:

options.A: Payments have been made to suppliers but the material has not been received or has not been linked, and the balances require follow-up and clearance
options.B: The depot is holding excess stock of stores
options.C: Scrap is awaiting survey and disposal in the depots
options.D: Suppliers' bills have not been paid at all

e: A debit balance under Purchase Suspense represents payments made to suppliers for which material has not been received or linked; long-outstanding debits therefore call for follow-up and clearance.

q: The maximum stock level fixed for a stores item principally serves the purpose of:

options.A: Guarding against over-stocking and the locking up of capital in stores
options.B: Ensuring that the stock never falls below the safety (buffer) level
options.C: Fixing the quantity to be ordered in a single purchase order
options.D: Determining the Average Annual Consumption of the item

e: The maximum stock level caps the quantity to be held at any time so that stock does not accumulate beyond requirements and capital is not locked up unnecessarily in stores.

q: A depot holds 1,850 units of an item. The book rate of the item is revised from Rs 96 to Rs 84 per unit. The decrease in the value of the stock in hand, which is adjusted through the Stock Adjustment Account, is:
e: Decrease in stock value = 1850 x (96 - 84) = 1850 x 12 = Rs 22,200, adjusted through the Stock Adjustment Account on revision of the book rate.

q: A depot proposes to condemn all the items shown as non-moving in its periodical list straightaway and sell them as scrap. The correct course is that:

options.A: The proposal is in order, non-moving items being straightaway condemned
options.B: Non-moving items are first reviewed, serviceable items usable elsewhere are transferred or declared surplus, and only items which are unserviceable are condemned and disposed of as scrap
options.C: The non-moving items are issued free of cost to the depot staff
options.D: The non-moving items are returned to the suppliers who supplied them

e: Non-moving items are not condemned straightaway; they are reviewed, serviceable items usable elsewhere are transferred or declared surplus, and only unserviceable items are surveyed, condemned and sold as scrap.

q: Stores purchased as non-stock items against the specific demand of a work or department are accounted for by:

options.A: Taking them into the priced stock of the depot like stock items
options.B: Crediting their value to Purchase Suspense
options.C: Including them in the closing balance of stores of the railway
options.D: Charging their cost direct to the work or department concerned, without routing them through the stock accounts

e: Non-stock stores bought against a specific demand are not taken into priced stock; their cost is charged direct to the work or department concerned on receipt.

q: Under the EOQ system with a uniform rate of consumption, the Economic Order Quantity of an item is 680 units. The average cycle stock of the item held is:
e: With uniform consumption, cycle stock rises to the EOQ and falls to zero, so average cycle stock = EOQ / 2 = 680 / 2 = 340 units.

q: While lying in a stores depot, the shelf life of a stock of rubber goods expires. Such stores:

options.A: Are issued on priority for immediate use
options.B: Are sold to railway employees at the book rate
options.C: Are re-tested and their shelf life extended by the depot officer
options.D: Cannot be issued for use and are dealt with as unserviceable stores, to be surveyed off

e: Stores whose shelf life has expired cannot be issued for use, since their quality is no longer assured; they are treated as unserviceable and surveyed off under the Stores Code.

q: The successful tenderer in a stores tender fails to accept the purchase order placed on him and also fails to furnish the prescribed Security Deposit. In such a case:

options.A: No action can be taken against him
options.B: The validity of his offer is automatically extended by one year
options.C: His earnest money is liable to be forfeited, and the Railway may place the order on another firm at his risk and cost
options.D: The Railway must pay him compensation for the trouble caused

e: A successful tenderer who fails to accept the order or furnish the Security Deposit forfeits his earnest money, and the Railway may place the order on another firm at his risk and cost under the IRS Conditions of Contract.

q: The total issues of stores of a railway during a year are to be worked out from its inventory turnover. The inventory turnover of the stores during the year is 8 times and the average stock held is Rs 72 lakh. The total issues of stores during the year are:
e: Inventory turnover = total issues / average stock, so total issues = 8 x Rs 72 lakh = Rs 576 lakh = Rs 5.76 crore.

q: At the Railway Board level, the stores balances and the Turnover Ratio of the zonal railways are watched and targets for them prescribed primarily as an instrument of:

options.A: Fixing the selling price of scrap
options.B: Determining the promotion of stores officers
options.C: Assessing the earnest money to be collected from tenderers
options.D: Inventory control, to keep the capital locked up in stores within reasonable limits

e: Stores balances and the Turnover Ratio are watched at Railway Board level as instruments of inventory control, to keep the capital locked up in stores within reasonable limits.

q: In the Balance Sheet of a railway, the value of the stores held in its depots is shown as:

options.D: It is not reflected in the Balance Sheet at all

e: Stores held in depots are an asset of the railway and the value of stock in hand is shown as such in its Balance Sheet.

q: Under a stores contract, stores of the value of Rs 3,60,000 remain in arrear of supply and are supplied 3 weeks and 2 days late. Liquidated damages at 0.5% of the value of the stores in arrear for each week or part of a week of delay amount to:
e: Delay of 3 weeks and 2 days counts as 4 weeks, part of a week being treated as a full week; LD = 0.5 per cent of 3,60,000 = Rs 1,800 per week x 4 = Rs 7,200, per the liquidated damages clause of the IRS Conditions of Contract.

q: On a review of the stock position of a depot, the stock of an item is found to be in excess of the maximum level fixed for it. The excess stock is treated as:

options.A: Over-stocking, to be reviewed for declaration as surplus

e: Stock held in excess of the fixed maximum level is over-stocking; it is reviewed and the excess is considered for declaration as surplus.

q: Through the depot module of the integrated Material Management System (iMMS), a stores depot can:

options.A: Record day-to-day receipts and issues of stores and obtain up-to-date stock balances of items
options.B: Pass suppliers' bills for payment on behalf of the Accounts Department
options.C: Conduct the e-auction of scrap lots
options.D: Fix the selling price of surplus stores

e: Through the depot module of iMMS the depot records day-to-day receipts and issues of stores and obtains up-to-date stock balances; bill passing, e-auction and price fixation are not depot module functions.

q: A stores depot issues 640 units of an item, whose book rate is Rs 75 per unit, to an outside party. Departmental charges are leviable at 15 per cent of the book value. The total amount recoverable from the party is:
e: Book value = 640 x 75 = Rs 48,000; departmental charges at 15 per cent = Rs 7,200; total recoverable = 48,000 + 7,200 = Rs 55,200, issues to outside parties being charged book value plus departmental charges.

q: Stores supplied against a purchase order were inspected before despatch and passed. On receipt at the consignee depot, however, they are found not to conform to the specification. The correct course for the consignee is to:

options.A: Accept the stores, pre-despatch inspection having already passed them
options.B: Reject the material, communicating the rejection to the supplier within the period stipulated in the contract through a rejection advice
options.C: Reject the material only after obtaining the approval of the Railway Board
options.D: Return the material at the Railway's cost without any rejection advice

e: Pre-despatch inspection does not bar rejection at destination; if stores do not conform to specification on receipt, the consignee rejects them through a rejection advice to the supplier within the period stipulated in the contract.

q: The quantity worked out as the Economic Order Quantity of a stores item is alternatively described as its:
e: The Economic Order Quantity is alternatively called the economic lot size, being the quantity per order that minimises the total of ordering and carrying costs.

q: The annual requirement of an item is 11,250 units and the quantity ordered each time (Economic Order Quantity) is 750 units. The number of orders to be placed during the year is:
e: Number of orders = annual requirement / EOQ = 11,250 / 750 = 15 orders.

q: Year after year, the Stock Adjustment Account of a railway closes with a larger debit balance than in the preceding year. Such a trend is viewed with concern because it points to:

options.A: Recurring losses and differences in stores accounting which require investigation and control
options.B: That the stores balance of the railway is increasing
options.C: That the Turnover Ratio of stores is improving
options.D: That purchases are being made at favourable rates

e: The Stock Adjustment Account absorbs losses, shortages and rate differences in stores accounting; a persistently growing debit balance points to recurring losses and differences needing investigation and control.

q: A stores tender cannot be decided within the validity period of the offers, and the tenderers are requested to extend the validity of their offers. One tenderer declines to extend the validity of his offer. In respect of that tenderer:

options.A: His earnest money is liable to be forfeited for declining the extension
options.B: He is entitled to the refund of his earnest money
options.C: His offer is deemed to stand extended for a further equal period
options.D: He is debarred from participating in future tenders of the railway

e: A tenderer who declines to extend the validity of his offer merely lets it lapse; no default is committed, so his earnest money is refunded and cannot be forfeited.

q: Stores tenders for a group of items were opened this morning in the purchase office. Before the offers are placed before the Tender Committee for its recommendations, the purchase office first prepares:

options.A: A comparative statement (tabulation) of the offers received
options.B: A purchase order on the lowest tenderer
options.C: A receipt note for the stores
options.D: A stock sheet of the depot balances

e: After tenders are opened, the purchase office first tabulates all offers in a comparative statement, which is then placed before the Tender Committee for its recommendations.

q: The annual consumption of an item is 2,450 units. The cost of placing one order is Rs 100 and the inventory carrying cost is Rs 4 per unit per year. The Economic Order Quantity of the item is:
e: EOQ = square root of (2 x 2450 x 100 / 4) = square root of 122,500 = 350 units.

q: A newly opened stores depot is being organised for the custody of its stock. Under the depot organisation followed on the Railways, the depot is divided into:

options.A: A single common godown in which all items are mixed together without separate custody
options.B: A separate depot for every individual item of stores
options.C: Offices only, the stores being kept with the consuming departments
options.D: Wards and sections, each ward holding a distinct group of stores in the custody of a storekeeper

e: A stores depot is organised into wards and sections, each ward holding a distinct group of stores in the custody of a storekeeper who is accountable for its balances.

q: A purchaser has been declared the successful bidder for a depot scrap lot of sale value up to Rs 3 lakh in an e-auction and has deposited the earnest money. The balance of the sale value of the lot is payable by him within:
e: Under the IREPS e-auction sale conditions, the balance sale value of a depot scrap lot up to Rs 3 lakh is payable within 10 days of acceptance of the bid (15 days for lots above Rs 3 lakh); the 40-day period is the free time allowed for taking delivery of depot scrap, not for payment (Answer: A).

q: A depot holds 350 units of an item at a book rate of Rs 18 per unit. A fresh receipt of 150 units is taken into stock at Rs 38 per unit. The revised book (average) rate of the item will be:
A stores matter pertaining to the depots of a division is to be dealt with by the head of the stores organisation at the divisional level. That officer is the:

options.D: Chief Materials Manager of the workshop

e: At the divisional level the stores organisation is headed by the Senior Divisional Materials Manager, who deals with stores matters of the depots in the division.

q: A depot classifies one of its stock items as a vital (safety) item and gives it priority in stocking. An item is treated as vital when:

options.A: It is the costliest item in stock
options.C: It is consumed daily in train operations
options.D: Its non-availability can affect the safe running of trains

e: An item is classified as vital when its non-availability can affect the safe running of trains, and such items are given priority in stocking and provisioning.

q: The AAC of an item is 6,300 units. The stock in hand is 525 units and the dues (quantity already on order) are 525 units. The coverage available for the item is:
e: Monthly consumption = 6300 / 12 = 525 units; coverage = (stock 525 + dues 525) / 525 = 1050 / 525 = 2 months.

q: In the working of a stores depot, the official in whose custody the stores are held and who is accountable for the balances held by him is known as the:
e: The official in whose custody stores are held and who is accountable for the balances with him is the Stockholder, who may be a storekeeper, an executive officer or another railway servant.

q: A supplier despatches stores against a purchase order and demands payment of his bill immediately on despatch. As a general rule, payment for stores purchased by the Railways is made:

options.A: In advance, on placement of the purchase order
options.B: On despatch of the material by the supplier
options.C: Only after receipt, inspection and acceptance of the stores at the destination
options.D: At the end of the financial year

e: As a general rule under the IRS Conditions of Contract, payment for stores is made only after the stores are received, inspected and accepted at destination.

q: The average consumption of an item is 48 units per day, the lead time for its procurement is 9 days and the safety (buffer) stock provided for it is 168 units. The re-order level of the item is:
e: Re-order level = average consumption x lead time + safety stock = 48 x 9 + 168 = 432 + 168 = 600 units.

q: Against indents already placed, a quantity of an item has been ordered on suppliers but has not yet been received in the depot. In stores parlance, this quantity on order is known as:
e: Quantity ordered on suppliers against indents but not yet received in the depot is known as dues, and stock plus dues together determine the coverage of an item.

q: The yearly statement of the Stock Adjustment Account of a railway forms an annexure to which of the following?

options.C: Finance Accounts of the Central Government

e: The yearly statement of the Stock Adjustment Account, showing the losses and differences adjusted during the year, forms an annexure to the Appropriation Accounts of the railway.

q: The re-order level of an item is 1,420 units and the re-order quantity is 880 units. The minimum consumption is 48 units per week and the minimum lead time is 5 weeks. The maximum stock level of the item is:
e: Maximum stock level = re-order level + re-order quantity - (minimum consumption x minimum lead time) = 1420 + 880 - (48 x 5) = 2300 - 240 = 2,060 units.

q: A field official is allowed to keep with him a fixed quantity of stores for meeting petty day-to-day requirements at his work site. Such stores held by him are known as:
e: Stores held by a field official in a fixed quantity for petty day-to-day requirements at the work site are imprest stores, accounted for against his imprest account.

q: A stores tender is invited for a purchase valued at Rs 90 lakh. For a tender of this value, the system of tendering mandatorily required is:
e: A purchase of Rs 90 lakh exceeds the prescribed high-value threshold (Rs 50 lakh) above which the two-packet (two-bid) system is mandatory, the techno-commercial bid being evaluated before the price bid is opened.

q: Under a stores contract, stores of the value of Rs 9,50,000 remain in arrear of supply and are supplied 5 weeks late. Liquidated damages at 0.5 per cent of the value of the stores in arrear for each week of delay amount to:
e: LD = 0.5 per cent of 9,50,000 = Rs 4,750 per week x 5 weeks = Rs 23,750, as per the liquidated damages clause of the stores contract.

q: In an e-auction of scrap, the bidding for a lot closes with a highest bid. The sale of the lot is treated as concluded:

options.A: The moment the highest bid is placed
options.B: As soon as any depot clerk notes the bid
options.C: Only after the highest bid is accepted by the competent authority
options.D: Only after approval of the Railway Board in every case

e: In an e-auction the highest bid alone does not conclude the sale; the lot is sold only when the highest bid is accepted by the competent authority.

q: Material is issued from a stores depot to a railway workshop for use on a manufacturing job in hand in the workshop. In the books, the value of the issue is initially debited to:
e: Material issued to a workshop for a manufacturing job is initially debited to Workshop Manufacturing Suspense, from which it is transferred to the cost of the job.

q: A supplier fails to supply 475 units of stores contracted at Rs 84 per unit. A risk purchase of the same quantity is made at Rs 103 per unit. The extra cost recoverable from the defaulting supplier is:
e: Extra cost of risk purchase = 475 x (103 - 84) = 475 x 19 = Rs 9,025, recoverable from the defaulting supplier under the risk purchase clause of the IRS Conditions of Contract.
